podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Authenticity vs. Manufacturing - Final Assessment
podcast.body: While her record label presented an overly dramatic and incredible story, and she wasn't entirely a "pre-fabricated character" like Rihanna, Lana Del Rey is described as a person with a complicated life whose mystical aesthetic, American Dream influences, and "over-the-top" persona largely existed before Polydor Records. Her story is a mix of authentic background and careful industry cultivation. "ella es una persona que tiene la vida bastante complicada, ha sido todo ese rollo místico de influencias de Dios, de sueños americanos, de rollo como un poco luego de ver, ya le venían de serio, de antes de entrar en polido de récords."

srcs.episode: Born to Die. El origen de Lana del Rey

podcast.title: Celebrity Association with Salem
podcast.body: Follana del Rey is one of the celebrities mentioned as having had relations with members of the band Salem. "Además de haber tenido relaciones con celibitiz como Julia Fox, Cornilo, Follana del Rey."

srcs.episode: Witch House: Cuando internet inventó su género maldito

podcast.title: Charitable Alignments
podcast.body: In addition to her direct philanthropic efforts, Lana Del Rey is also aligned with Liverpool of the Premier League and their various charities. "Plus, she's also aligned with Liverpool of the Premier League and their charities."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaborator with Sean Lennon
podcast.body: Lana Del Rey has collaborated with Sean Lennon on records. "Lana Del Rey."

podcast.title: Convergence of Female Artists
podcast.body: Lana Del Rey is mentioned as one of several contemporary female artists who, along with Florence + The Machine, Sia, Adele, Lorde, and Lady Gaga, are perceived to be converging stylistically due to their reliance on the same professional lyricists and producers. "el que produjo a Lana del Rey."

srcs.episode: LANZAMIENTOS JUNIO 2018

podcast.title: Country Music Influence
podcast.body: Lana del Rey is mentioned as one of the artists currently creating music inspired by the Country genre. "Artistas como Lana del Rey [...] sacando canciones, guaciendo colaboraciones con músicos del género."

srcs.episode: El genio roto del country: La leyenda de Hank Williams

podcast.title: Delayed Vinyl Release
podcast.body: The vinyl edition of Lana del Rey's latest album experienced a delay, despite the album being available in compact disc and digital formats, before its eventual release in September. "la edición en Vinilo se demoraba y a saldrá este mes de septiembre."

srcs.episode: Lanzamientos de Septiembre 2017

podcast.title: Engineered Virality of "Video Games"
podcast.body: The viral success of the "Video Games" video on YouTube was not entirely organic. It was a "highly orchestrated viral event," with significant funding from her record label for paid promotions on Facebook and various other pages, and industry insiders actively retweeting and sharing the video to give it momentum. "fue un sitio viral, pero fue un sitio viral muy recombucido, tampoco os creéis que salió de la nada."

srcs.episode: Born to Die. El origen de Lana del Rey

podcast.title: Evolving Social Views and Activism
podcast.body: After an initially "rocky relationship with the concept of feminism," Lana Del Rey has voiced support for third-wave feminism. She is fiercely anti-Trump and has engaged in hands-on activism, working at homeless shelters and helping to build homes for the Navajo nation. "After a rocky relationship with the concept of feminism, she has voiced support for third wave feminism. She's fiercely anti-Trump. She's taken time to work at homeless shelters and help build homes for the Navajo nation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Extensive Production for Debut Material
podcast.body: Contrary to a low-budget image, "Video Games" and "Born to Die" (both single and album) were recorded simultaneously with immense resources. The "Born to Die" album, specifically, involved eight different producers, each more expensive and renowned than the last, highlighting a substantial financial and resource investment. "el famoso Borto de la Inenana del Rey, tienen 8 productores distintos, pero no es solo que tengan 8 productores, sino que cada uno de ellos es más caro, más importante y más cotizado del anterior."

srcs.episode: Born to Die. El origen de Lana del Rey

podcast.title: Femme Fatale Image and Dreamy Sound
podcast.body: Lana Del Rey is noted for her "femme fatale" image and a dreamy quality in her music, even though it may lack the dense layers of guitars and synths typically associated with Dreampop. Some of her music fits the description of the genre.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Dreampop - A History

podcast.title: Genre Fluidity and Influences
podcast.body: Her music has shifted across many styles, including pop, rock, dream pop, psych, trip pop, and trap. Listeners can discern the "ghost" of iconic vocalists like Nina Simone, Frank Sinatra, Billie Holiday, and various torch singers in her sound. "If you close your eyes, you can hear the ghost of Nina Simone, Frank Sinatra, Billie Holiday, and any number of torch singers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Justin Parker's Personal Investment
podcast.body: Justin Parker demonstrated his strong belief in Lana Del Rey by making a significant personal investment. He contributed $10,000 from his own pocket on the first day to support her initial improvements and extensively rewrote her existing songs with professional writers to enhance their aesthetic and narrative depth. "Justin Parker ya os dice la muerte, y se casca un atentico de inmigual de su propio bolsillo, y ya le da 10 mil parros con tantas y sonantes en el primer día."

srcs.episode: Born to Die. El origen de Lana del Rey

podcast.title: Justin Parker's Strategic Vision
podcast.body: Justin Parker, a prominent music executive ("Idol Maker"), was not hesitant about Lana Del Rey. He sought artists to fill the niche of "independent or indie soloists" that Polydor felt was underserved compared to their roster of commercial stars like Rihanna. He saw Lana Del Rey's mystical, "dark" aesthetic as perfect for this role. "no terminaba de ver, es gente que cobría ese bien el hueco de las solistas independientes o del rollo Indy."

srcs.episode: Born to Die. El origen de Lana del Rey

podcast.title: Marketing Strategy Behind "Lana Del Rey" Name
podcast.body: The official stories Lana Del Rey provided in interviews about the origin of her stage name – either hearing an old radio announcer say "The Lana Del Rey" or her Cuban friends in Miami calling her that – were debunked. The name "Lana Del Rey" was a marketing creation by Polydor Records, chosen for its ease and profitability as an artist brand. "no realmente en la Ana de Rihanna es una colombia de marketing, en el cual Polidor Records llegó a la comisión de que era el nombre más fácil y más rentable para tenerla como artista."

srcs.episode: Born to Die. El origen de Lana del Rey

podcast.title: Official vs. Rectified Biography - Early Life
podcast.body: The official narrative stated Lana Del Rey had a difficult adolescence, becoming an alcoholic at 14 and being sent to a recluse boarding school from 15 to 18 to overcome the problem. This was later rectified; while she was a rebellious and problematic teenager who drank alcohol, there is no medical record or evidence she was treated for alcoholism at any stage, especially not as a teenager. "en contra de lo que nos metieron, no fue al colo con 14 años. Sí es verdad, que fue una persona con muchos problemas de comportamiento, ella era una amiga rebelde, ella se portaba muy mal, se esterraba de casa a menudo, bebía al colo, el social es verdad, bebía bastante al colo, como adolescente."

srcs.episode: Born to Die. El origen de Lana del Rey

podcast.title: Official vs. Rectified Biography - Education
podcast.body: Lana Del Rey's official biography initially stated she studied "professional metaphysics" at New York University, a claim that surprised many because such studies do not exist. This was corrected to "philosophy with a specialization in heterodox mysticism," which was also later found to be untrue. She did enroll in the philosophy faculty at NYU and took some related courses but did not complete her degree. "Ella estudió, pero esto es profesionales de metafísima universidad, porque realmente son estudios que ni siquiera existen."

srcs.episode: Born to Die. El origen de Lana del Rey

podcast.title: Official vs. Rectified Biography - Family Relationships
podcast.body: The official story claimed her relationships with her parents deteriorated after her time in boarding school, leading her to live with her uncles upon her return to New York. This was later debunked, as it was revealed her father provided significant financial support for her early recordings before she signed with Polydor, indicating a good relationship. "su padre le dio bastante dinero para ayudar a sus primeras grabaciones antes de fechar por polido."

srcs.episode: Born to Die. El origen de Lana del Rey

podcast.title: Ongoing Criticism and Immense Influence
podcast.body: Despite her charitable work and evolving social views, Lana Del Rey remains subject to criticism, primarily regarding the themes and imagery present in her music. Nevertheless, her influence on contemporary artists such as Billie Eilish, Lorde, and Halsey is considered immense. "Even with all that, Lana is subject to all sorts of criticism, mostly over the themes and imagery in her music. At the same time, though, her influence has been immense. Could there have been a Billie Eilish or Lord or Halsey without Lana Del Rey? I'd say no."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Polarizing Artistic Style
podcast.body: Since her emergence in 2005, Lana Del Rey has been a polarizing artist, largely due to her distinctive musical style. Her sound is often described as reminiscent of Hollywood from the 1950s and 1960s, a style sometimes labeled "Hollywood Sadcore." "Lana Del Rey has been polarizing as an artist. Ever since we first started hearing about her in 2005, mostly because of her musical style, which is somehow reminiscent of Hollywood from the 50s and 60s. In fact, her music has been described as Hollywood Sadcore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Previous Artist Names and Material Deletion
podcast.body: Before achieving fame as Lana Del Rey, she registered the name Elizabeth Grant (though she never performed under it), performed and released material as Lizzy Grant, and later as May Jailer. After signing with Polydor, a deliberate and active effort was made by Justin Parker to erase all this prior material, buying rights from previous producers and Facebook Records in a multi-million dollar agreement. All content, including published recordings and fan-made videos, was removed from platforms like iTunes and YouTube. "Él fue y recorrió toda la gente que tenía derechos compartidos, con Ana del Rey, sus caceriores trabajos, que casi todo era Facebook Records, que lo van a acuerdo multimillonario para cogerlo todo... y lo moraron todo del marco, se cargaron todo, sacaron todo el iTunes."

srcs.episode: Born to Die. El origen de Lana del Rey

podcast.title: Professional Development and Training
podcast.body: The official story claimed Lana Del Rey fell in love with London and often visited. In reality, Justin Parker took her to London specifically for intensive professional training in singing and corporal expression, intending to shape her into a fully-fledged artist. "Ya sin parque se llevó a Ana de Rihanna, a Londres, para tener clases profesionales de canto, de expresión corporal, todas estas cosas para ser una artista de hacha y derecha."

srcs.episode: Born to Die. El origen de Lana del Rey

podcast.title: Public Image and Perceived Authenticity
podcast.body: Lana Del Rey's public persona has been marked by a dichotomy between tragic personal stories and criticisms that she is a "pre-fabricated marketing product." There has been considerable debate regarding where the "myth" of Lana Del Rey ends and the real person, Elizabeth Grant, begins. "por un lado tenemos, esos historias suficientes que son como muy tráficas, y por el otro lado tenemos un montón de gente de la industria musical que dice que hay prácticamente un producto perfabricado del marketing."

xref.title: Broad Influence on Contemporary Artists
xref.body: Her distinctive style and sound have had a profound impact on a wide range of artists across different genres. Influences can be heard in the music of Florence Welch (Florence + The Machine), Lady Gaga, Lana Del Rey, Alessia Cara, and Billie Eilish. Male singers such as Bruno Mars and Sam Smith also credit Amy as an inspiration. "Her influence can be heard in the music of any number of artists. Florence Welch or Florence in the machine. Lady Gaga, Lana Del Rey, Alissa Carrier and Billie Eilish."

xref.title: Diverse Musical Career
xref.body: Sean Lennon, the son of John Lennon and Yoko Ono, has had a varied musical career. He has been a member of multiple bands, composed scores for films, produced material for other artists, and released several solo albums. He has also collaborated with prominent figures such as Albert Hammond Jr. of The Strokes, The Flaming Lips, Lady Gaga, and Lana Del Rey. "Sean Lennon is the son of John and Yoko. He's been in a bunch of different bands, scored some films, produced material for other people, recorded a couple of albums on his own, and collaborated on records with people like Albert Hammond Jr. of the Strokes, The Flaming Lips, Lady Gaga, and Lana Del Rey."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Shirley Manson's Influence
xref.body: Shirley Manson, the Scottish singer drafted into the American band Garbage, has had a notable impact on contemporary artists. Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evanescence, Katy Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish, and Lana Del Rey. "Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evan Essence, Katie Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish and Lana Del Rey."
